chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
Whoever drinks from the wine a single drink, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of drinking wine on the acceptance of prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the spiritual consequence of consuming khamr, linking the physical act to a forty-day period of rejected prayers. This ruling highlights the severity of wine consumption in Shia jurisprudence, where even a single sip incurs a temporary suspension of the validity of salah, emphasizing the need for repentance to restore one's spiritual state.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The one who drinks from the wine a drink, a Prayer would not be Accepted from him for forty days’.
en.sarwar: 5. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one drinks one sip of wine his Salat (prayer) is not accepted forty days.’”
